newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas narrowly mixed late, stuck in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas narrowly mixed late, stuck in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were narrowly mixed late Monday in sluggish trade, with a steady cash in the face of more hot weather this week keeping prices in recent technical ranges, market sources said.
At 1425 EDT, August was off 0.4 cent at $2.135 per million British thermal units, while September was unchanged at $2.14. Other deferreds were trading on either side of unchanged.

"The market is somewhat in equilibrium. I don't think there's much you can do with these numbers, technically or fundamentally," said one New York trader, noting activity was likely to remain slow this week ahead of the July 4 holiday.

With bidweek now over, many opted for the sidelines waiting for clearer signs from the cash when July flows begin Tuesday. But few had strong convictions about market direction, with forecasts for more heat this week partly offset by the Independence Day holiday and some early-July industrial shutdowns.

Temperatures in the South and East are expected to remain above normal this week, with Texas forecast to return to about normal later in the week. The Southwest was expected to stay hot for the period.

Chart traders, citing the symmetrical triangle formation in August, saw support along the up trendline in the $2.11 area, with trendline resistance at $2.27. More buying was expected at the recent $2.08 low, while further selling should emerge at the recent $2.36 high and the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Monday, Gulf Coast prices notionally were steady to up slightly in the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes firmed a couple of cents to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas for July was quoted steady in the mid-$2.40s.
Separately, the 1,250 megawatt South Texas 1 nuclear unit was reduced to about 69 percent power over the weekend for repairs, while Entergy Corp's 836 MW Arkansas 1 unit was cut to 55 percent.
NYMEX said 9,181 contracts traded at 1355 EDT.
On KCBT, August eased one-half cent to $2.01, while deferreds were unchanged. The August East/West spread widened by 0.1 cent to 12.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
